 Oral Judgment
(Per: The Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Vijaykumar A.Patil)

This appeal is filed by the insurance company challenging the liability as well as quantum of compensation being aggrieved by judgment and award dated 11.09.2018 passed in MVC No.80/2015 on the file of learned Senior Civil Judge and MACT, Kushtagi1.
2.

Brief facts leading to filing of this appeal are that the claimants filed a claim petition before the Tribunal seeking compensation for the accidental death of Malleshappa Badiger on 16.06.2010 involving motorcycle bearing registration No.KA- 37/Q-5824 and Cruiser vehicle bearing registration No.KA- 27/A-0325.
The deceased Malleshappa Badiger was aged about 30 years, was doing carpentry work and earning Rs.10,000/- per month.
3. The respondent No.3/Insurer appeared before the Tribunal and filed statement of objections denying the age, income and avocation of the deceased.
It was contended that the driver of the offending vehicle was not holding valid and 'Tribunal', for short NC: 2024:KHC-D:13075-DB effective driving license as on the date of the accident.
It was further contended that due to rash and negligent riding of rider of the motorcycle, the accident took place.
Thus, sought dismissal of claim petition.

On appreciation of entire evidence on record, the Tribunal allowed the claim petition in part awarding a total compensation of Rs.15,77,000/- with interest at the rate of 8% per annum by holding that the respondent No.3/insurer is liable to pay compensation amount and recover the same from the owner of the offending vehicle.
Aggrieved by the same, the insurer is in appeal.

4. Sri.S.K. Kayakamath, learned counsel appearing for the appellant/Insurer strenuously contends that the Tribunal committed an error in recording a finding of 'Pay and Recovery', inasmuch as the driver of the offending vehicle was not having valid and effective driving license as on the date of the accident.

He further submits that the driver of the offending vehicle was having DL to drive non-transport vehicle, but the vehicle involved in the accident in question is a transport vehicle,
hence, the entire liability is to be fixed on the driver of the offending vehicle by directing the owner to pay compensation.

It is submitted that the Tribunal committed a NC: 2024:KHC-D:13075-DB grave error in assessing the income of the deceased at Rs.8,000/- per month, in the absence of any cogent and acceptable evidence on record.

It is further submitted that since the deceased was a carpenter and as per notional income chart of KSLSA, the notional income of the deceased would be Rs.5,500/- per month for the accident of the year 2010.
He further submits that the Tribunal also erred in awarding interest at the rate of 8% per annum and it requires to be reduced to 6% per annum.
Thus, he seeks to allow the appeal by awarding compensation appropriately.

sentences.text: Per contra, learned counsel Sri. Hanumanthreddy Sahukar, for the respondents/claimants supports the impugned judgment and award and submits that the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and proper, which requires no interference at the hands of this Court.
Thus, he prays for dismissal of the appeal.
6. We have heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the material available on record.

The point that arises for consideration in this appeal is, whether the impugned NC:
2024:KHC-D:13075-DB judgment and award of the Tribunal calls for interference at the hands of this Court?
7.
The parties to the proceedings do not dispute the occurrence of accident on 16.06.2010 resulting in death of deceased Malleshappa Badiger.
It is also not in dispute that the deceased Malleshappa was doing carpentry work and aged about 31 years at the time of the accident.
8. The insurance company contended that the driver of the offending vehicle was not having driving license to drive Transport vehicle, but he was having DL to drive non-transport vehicle.

The said issue is no more res-integra in view of decision of the Apex Court in the case of Mukund Dewangan Vs. Oriental Insurance Company Limited2, wherein it has held that the driver of the vehicle, who possesses DL to drive non-transport vehicle is also eligible to drive Transport vehicle.

entities.text: Mukund Dewangan Vs. Oriental Insurance Company Limited2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The finding of the Tribunal that the insurance company is liable to pay compensation at the first instance and then recover the same from the owner of the offending vehicle, on the ground that driver of the offending vehicle was not having valid permit AIR 2017 SC 3668 NC: 2024:KHC-D:13075-DB at the relevant point of time, is based on oral and documentary evidence available on record.

The said finding,
which in our view, is just and appropriate and the same is affirmed holding that the insurance company is liable to pay compensation at the first instance and then recover the same from the owner of the offending vehicle.
9. The Tribunal assessed the income of the deceased at Rs.8,000/- per month, which is on the higher side.
Admittedly, the deceased was a carpenter and no cogent and acceptable evidence is placed on record.
In the absence of any documentary evidence on record, this Court assesses the income notionally based on income chart prepared by the KSLSA.
However, the deceased was a carpenter and the accident of the year 2010.

Taking note of the avocation, age and nature of job,
which the deceased was doing, we are of the considered view that it would be just and appropriate to re- assess the income of the deceased at Rs.6,000/- per month.
There is no dispute with regard to age of deceased as 31 appropriate multiplier of 16 and deduction of 1/4th towards personal and living expenses of the deceased, as there are five dependents.

Since the deceased was below the age of 40 NC: 2024:KHC-D:13075-DB years, the claimants would be entitled to an addition of 40% of the assessed income towards loss of future prospects of the deceased.

Thus, loss of dependency is recalculated as under:
Rs.6,000 + 40% x 12 x 16 x 3/4 = Rs. 12,09,600/-
10.

The claimants being wife, minor children and mother of the deceased would be entitled to Rs.44,000/- each towards loss of consortium, besides Rs.16,500/- towards loss of estate and M/S. Cholamandalam M S General ... vs Smt. Ratna W/O. Late Malleshappa ...

4 Rs.16,500/- towards funeral expenses.

Thus, in all, the claimants would be entitled to modified compensation as under:
 Loss of dependency Rs.12,09,600/-
 Loss of consortium Rs. 2,20,000/-
 Loss of estate & funeral expensesRs. 33,000/-
 ------------------
 Total Rs.14,62,600/-
 ------------------
11.
Thus, the claimants would be entitled to total compensation of Rs.14,62,600/- as against Rs.15,77,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.
12. The Tribunal committed an error in granting interest at the rate of 8% per annum on the compensation amount.

Taking note of present bank's rate of interest, we incline to NC:
2024:KHC-D:13075-DB reduce the rate of interest to 6% from 8% on the entire compensation amount.

13. In the result, we proceed to pass the following:
ORDER a) The appeal stands allowed in part.
b) The impugned judgment and award of the Tribunal is modified holding that the claimants are entitled to total compensation of Rs.14,62,600/- as against Rs.15,77,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.
c) The entire compensation amount shall carry interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till realization.
d) The appellant/insurer shall deposit the aforesaid amount with accrued interest before the Tribunal within a period of eight weeks from the date of receipt of certified copy of this judgment.
e) The apportionment, deposit and disbursement shall be made as per award of the Tribunal.
f) The amount in deposit be transmitted to the Tribunal forthwith.

h) Draw modified award accordingly.
i) No order as to costs.
